rows.answer: For standard reimbursement claims, you must submit the claim within 30 days of discharge [1][2], whereas under Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission window is 60 days from discharge [5]. Additionally, the sources note a conflict with an archived 2024 guideline, which previously stated the deadline was 15 days from discharge [3].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on retail plans, unless explicitly waived in writing on the policy schedule by Aurora [3][5]. However, under the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above, the pre-existing disease waiting period is 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][5].

As of 1 April 2026, Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1]. Because hospitals join and leave the network continuously, the authoritative list is maintained in the hospital locator on the Aurora app and portal [1].

Under Aurora Gold, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. A claim does not reduce the accumulated bonus; it only stops accumulation for that specific year [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment, as infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are listed as permanent exclusions [1].
Under the Aurora Gold plan, the sub-limit for cataract surgery is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome, you can escalate the matter to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

Across all plans, road ambulance cover is ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, under the Aurora Gold plan, air ambulance is covered up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India, subject to prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The 30-day initial waiting period applies, with no separate waiting period required [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [3]. A new policyholder may cancel within 15 days of receiving the policy document, or within 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. Upon cancellation during this period, the premium is refunded minus proportionate risk premium for the cover period, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You earn 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is explicitly not considered a day-care procedure [3].
For a cashless emergency admission, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][5].
No, Aurora does not use a TPA [1]. Aurora administers its own claims directly [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, everything will not be paid [1][5]. Under the Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, the room-rent limit is 2% of the sum insured (₹10,000 per day) [1][2]. Because the room cost of ₹15,000 per day exceeds this limit, an eligibility ratio of 0.667 is applied, leading to proportionate deductions across multiple billed expenses [1][5].

Dependent parents can be covered under the Silver plan (at an extra premium), Gold plan, and Platinum plan, but not under the Bronze plan [1]. Adding a parent changes how the premium is calculated, as it is determined by the age of the eldest member covered; this often makes adding them to a floater more expensive than buying an individual senior-citizen policy, and advisers must present both options in writing [4].

Waiting periods already served with your previous insurer will carry over, but only up to the sum insured of your previous policy, including its accrued no-claim bonus [1][2]. Any increase in the sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods on the incremental amount [1][2].

To continue your baby's cover beyond the initial 90 days, you must inform Aurora within 90 days of birth to add the newborn as a dependent with guaranteed-issue cover and no medical underwriting [1]. Additionally, if you are filing a reimbursement claim for the delivery or hospitalisation, you must submit the claim within 30 days of discharge [3].

Under the Aurora Silver plan, a claim reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points [1]. It does not reset your accumulated bonus to zero [1].
Under the Gold plan, the maternity limit for a caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 per delivery [1]. If the hospital bills ₹1,60,000, your out-of-pocket cost would be ₹60,000 [1].

Knee joint replacement is only covered immediately (with no waiting period) if it is required following an accident [1][5]. Otherwise, knee joint replacement has a 24-month waiting period before it becomes payable [1][5].
Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium [1]. The wellness discount (which is up to 15% at renewal) is applied last, after the cap, and is the only discount that may exceed it [1][3][5].

For general reimbursement claims, you have 45 days from the date of the query to respond, after which Aurora closes the claim [2][5]. However, for motor insurance claims, the deadline to submit a response to an Aurora query is 30 days from the date of the query [4].

The sources conflict on the required timeline. Under the archived 2024 rules, a planned cashless admission must be notified 48 hours before admission [1], whereas current sources state that the notification or pre-authorisation request must be submitted at least 72 hours before admission [2][3].

Across Aurora's four health indemnity plans, pre-hospitalisation cover spans 30 days, 45 days, 60 days, and 90 days respectively [1][3]. In comparison, post-hospitalisation cover is provided for 60 days, 90 days, 120 days, and 180 days across the plans [1].

You should choose the Gold plan, as it removes room-rent sub-limits [3] and covers dependent parents-in-law [1]. While the Platinum plan also covers dependent parents-in-law [1], the provided sources do not specify its room-rent sub-limit terms.

Dental treatment and oral surgery are permanently excluded under any Aurora indemnity plan, unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [2][3]. Additionally, out-patient dental work is not covered by any plan [1].
